# Exporting {#sec-exporting}

A project's pages can be exported to several formats.
To export a project, click the **File** tab and select **Export**.
From here, select the export format and click its export button.

The following formats are available:

- **HTML Dashboard**: An interactive dashboard that opens in any web browser.
- **PDF**: A document that is easy to share and print.
- **PowerPoint**: A *PowerPoint* (`.pptx`) presentation.
- **OpenDocument Presentation**: An *OpenDocument* (`.odp`) presentation, which opens in *LibreOffice Impress* and other presentation software.
- **SVG**: A single SVG file containing all the pages.

Each format has its own options dialog, which is described below.
Your selections in these dialogs are saved with the project.

## Exporting a Graph {#sec-export-graph}

If a graph from the [**Graphs**](#sec-graphs-section) section is selected, then the **Export** page also has a **Selected Graph** section.
This section is shown above the project's export formats, which are listed under **Project**.
Click **Export Graph** to save the graph as an image.
You will be asked for the image format (e.g., PNG, SVG, or PDF), and then where to save the file.

## Pages to Export {#sec-export-page-selection}

If a project has more than one page, then a list of its pages is shown before the export options.
Check the pages to include in the export.

**Select All**: Click this button to check every page.

**Select None**: Click this button to uncheck every page.

::: {.notesection data-latex=""}
At least one page must be checked to continue.
The pages that you leave unchecked are remembered for the next export to the same format.
:::

\newpage

## HTML Export Options {#sec-export-html}

The options in this dialog customize the exported HTML dashboard.

### Document Information {-}

**Title**: Enter the title of the dashboard.
If this is left empty, then the label of the first page is used.

**Subject**: Enter the subject of the dashboard.
This is written as the web page's description.

**Author**: Enter the author of the dashboard.

**Keywords**: Enter keywords that describe the dashboard.

::: {.notesection data-latex=""}
The title, subject, author, and keywords are shared with the project's [settings](#sec-project-settings).
Changing them here will also update the project.
:::

**Logo**: Select an image to show in the dashboard's title bar.
Leave this empty to not show a logo.

**Theme**: Select the theme to style the dashboard with.

### Page Size {-}

**Page width**: Enter the width (in pixels) that every page is rendered at.

**Page height**: Enter the height (in pixels) that every page is rendered at.

### Display {-}

:::: {.optionssection data-latex=""}
::: {.optionssectiontitle data-latex=""}
Initial View
:::

Select how the pages are presented when the dashboard is first opened:

**Gallery**: Small page cards are shown across the top, with the selected page shown below them.

**Slideshow**: Full-height pages are shown in a scrolling column.
::::

**Include color mode toggle**: Check this option to include a toggle that switches the dashboard between **Auto**, **Light**, and **Dark** modes.

:::: {.optionssection data-latex=""}
::: {.optionssectiontitle data-latex=""}
Initial Color Mode
:::

Select the light or dark mode that the dashboard opens in:

**Auto**: Follows the operating system's setting.

**Light**: Always opens in light mode.

**Dark**: Always opens in dark mode.
::::

**Count up large numbers**: Check this option to have large numbers count up when a page is revealed.

**Include dual layout orientations**: Check this option to also render each page with its width and height swapped.
The browser will then show whichever orientation best fits its window.

### Buttons {-}

**Include Save button**: Check this option to include a **Save** button in the dashboard.

**Include Print button**: Check this option to include a **Print** button in the dashboard.

**Include Copy button**: Check this option to include a **Copy** button in the dashboard.

### Filtering {-}

**Include group visibility toggles**: Check this option to include checkboxes that hide or show a graph's groups.

::: {.notesection data-latex=""}
The choices for filterable graphs are always included, regardless of this option.
:::

**Remember filter choices and group visibility in browser**: Check this option to have the browser remember the filter choices and hidden groups between visits.

**Filter Defaults**: If the project contains filterable graphs, then this section lists each dataset and column that the graphs are filtered by.
Select the choice that each filter should open on.

\newpage

## PDF Export Options {#sec-export-pdf}

The options in this dialog customize the exported PDF document.

### Page {-}

**Page Setup...**: Click this button to select the paper size and orientation.

**Paper type**: Shows the selected paper size.

**Orientation**: Shows the selected paper orientation (i.e., portrait or landscape).

### Document Information {-}

**Title**: Enter the title of the document.

**Author**: Enter the author of the document.

**Subject**: Enter the subject of the document.

**Keywords**: Enter keywords that describe the document.

::: {.notesection data-latex=""}
The title, subject, author, and keywords are shared with the project's [settings](#sec-project-settings).
Changing them here will also update the project.
:::

**Compress content**: Check this option to compress the PDF's content, which will make the file smaller.

\newpage

## PowerPoint Export Options {#sec-export-pptx}

The options in this dialog customize the exported *PowerPoint* presentation.

### Slide Size {-}

:::: {.optionssection data-latex=""}
::: {.optionssectiontitle data-latex=""}
Preset
:::

**Widescreen (16:9)**: Creates slides that are 13.333 × 7.5 inches.

**Standard (4:3)**: Creates slides that are 10 × 7.5 inches.

**Custom**: Creates slides with the width and height entered below.
::::

**Width (inches)**: Enter the width of the slides.
This is only available when **Custom** is selected.

**Height (inches)**: Enter the height of the slides.
This is only available when **Custom** is selected.

::: {.notesection data-latex=""}
A slide's width and height cannot be larger than 56 inches.
:::

### Document Information {-}

**Title**: Enter the title of the presentation.

**Author**: Enter the author of the presentation.

**Subject**: Enter the subject of the presentation.

**Keywords**: Enter keywords that describe the presentation.

**Publisher**: Enter the publisher of the presentation.

**Include a title slide**: Check this option to add a title slide before the project's pages.
The title slide shows the presentation's title, with the author beneath it.
If a publisher is entered, then it is shown at the bottom of the slide.

**Theme**: Select a color scheme for the title slide.
When a color scheme is selected, the title slide will have a gradient background, an accent bar, a decorative accent circle, and themed text colors.
Select **None** to use a plain title slide.

### Transitions {-}

**Effect**: Select the transition effect used between slides.
The available effects are **None**, **Fade**, **Push**, **Wipe**, **Split**, **Cut**, and **Morph**.

**Speed**: Select how quickly the transition plays (**Slow**, **Medium**, or **Fast**).

**Advance on mouse click**: Check this option to advance to the next slide when the mouse is clicked.

**Advance automatically after [5] seconds**: Check this option to advance to the next slide automatically.
Enter the number of seconds that each slide is shown.

**Loop continuously until Esc**: Check this option to have the slideshow start over after its last slide.
The slideshow will continue until `r keys("Esc")` is pressed.

### Notes {-}

**Add chart descriptions as speaker notes**: Check this option to add descriptions of each slide's charts as speaker notes.
These descriptions come from the page's titles and the accessibility descriptions of its objects.

## ODP Export Options {#sec-export-odp}

The options in this dialog customize the exported *OpenDocument* presentation.
These options are the same as the [**PowerPoint Export Options**](#sec-export-pptx), except for the following:

- **Advance on mouse click** is not available.
- **Loop continuously until Esc** is not available.

\newpage

## SVG Export Options {#sec-export-svg}

The options in this dialog customize the exported SVG file.

### Page Size {-}

**Use page setup**: Select this option to size the pages from a paper size and orientation.

**Page Setup...**: Click this button to select the paper size and orientation.

**Paper type**: Shows the selected paper size.

**Orientation**: Shows the selected paper orientation (i.e., portrait or landscape).

**Custom size**: Select this option to enter the page size yourself.

**Width**: Enter the width (in pixels) of the pages.
This is only available when **Custom size** is selected.

**Height**: Enter the height (in pixels) of the pages.
This is only available when **Custom size** is selected.

A preview of the page's shape (i.e., its aspect ratio) is shown next to these options.

### Interactive Features {-}

**Layout options**: Check this option to include a floating toggle that switches between the page layouts.
A spinner for adjusting the gap between pages is also included.

:::: {.optionssection data-latex=""}
::: {.optionssectiontitle data-latex=""}
Default Page Layout
:::

Select how the pages are laid out when the file is opened.
This is only available when **Layout options** is checked.

**Single**: The pages are shown in a single column.

**Duplex**: The pages are shown side by side.

**Stacked**: The pages are stacked on top of each other, each one offset to the lower right.
::::

**Dark mode toggle**: Check this option to include a floating toggle that switches between light and dark mode.

**Slideshow navigation**: Check this option to include slideshow navigation.
This adds previous and next buttons, and lets the arrow keys move between pages.

**Transitions**: Check this option to have pages slide smoothly when moving between them.

**Page shadow**: Check this option to draw a subtle shadow under each page.

**Layer controls**: Check this option to include checkboxes that hide or show the pages in each layer.
These are only included if a page is assigned to a layer.

**Hover highlighting**: Check this option to highlight objects when the mouse moves over them.

**Theme**: Select the theme that the colors of the buttons and effects come from.

\newpage

## Image Export Options {#sec-export-image}

When you save a page as an image, you will first be asked to select an image format.
The following formats are available:

- **PNG** (Portable Network Graphics): A lossless-compressed format.
  The image can be compressed to a smaller size without any loss of quality.
- **JPG** (Joint Photographic Experts Group): A lossy-compressed format.
  Some image quality may be lost, compared to formats such as PNG.
- **BMP** (Bitmap): An uncompressed raster (i.e., pixel based) format.
- **TIFF** (Tagged Image File Format): A format that can be compressed or uncompressed.
  It offers both lossy and lossless compression and is generally preferred for desktop publishing.
- **TARGA** (Truevision Advanced Raster Graphics Adapter): A raster (i.e., pixel based) format.
- **GIF** (Graphics Interchange Format): A raster (i.e., pixel based) format.
  This format is limited to 256 colors.
- **SVG** (Scalable Vector Graphics): A format that uses vector (rather than raster) drawing.
  Vector-based images can be scaled to much larger sizes, without the loss of quality that raster images would experience.
- **WebP** (Web Picture): A replacement for JPEG, PNG, and GIF which supports both lossy and lossless compression.
- **PDF** (Portable Document Format): A vector-based document format that preserves text and graphics at any scale.

After selecting a format, the **Image Export Options** dialog is shown.
(If you selected **PDF**, then the [**PDF Export Options**](#sec-export-pdf) dialog is shown instead.)

### Image Size {-}

**Width**: Enter the width (in pixels) of the image.

**Height**: Enter the height (in pixels) of the image.

The width and height are linked, so changing one will adjust the other to keep the image's aspect ratio.
Both can range from 128 to 10000 pixels.

:::: {.optionssection data-latex=""}
::: {.optionssectiontitle data-latex=""}
Color Mode
:::

**RGB (Color)**: Select this option to save the image in color.

**Grayscale**: Select this option to save the image in shades of gray.

These options are not available for SVG.
::::

### TIFF Options {-}

**Compression**: Select the compression method for the image.
The available methods are **None**, **Lempel-Ziv & Welch**, **JPEG**, and **Deflate**.

This option is only available for TIFF.

### Preview {-}

A preview of the image is shown on the right side of the dialog.
It updates as you change the color mode.
